mutant.description: FOUR SHAPED NEGATIVE CONTROLS PER CARD against the ACTUAL v3.1 schema, each aimed at a DIFFERENT v3.1-specific requirement so a positive cannot come from a validator that accepts anything: (1) schema_version -> 1, the legacy v1 const, which is the exact failure that caused two cards on the sibling face to be validated against the wrong contract; (2) an out-of-enum value on a required enum field; (3) drop a required leaf (trust.failure_mode.owner); (4) re-introduce prose into an id field, which the schema forbids by pattern. PLUS THREE UNPLANNED LIVE MUTANTS THAT I DID NOT DESIGN AND THAT ARE BETTER EVIDENCE THAN THE ONES I DID: I invented three enum members while authoring -- live_matches_declared='partial' on card 3, and materializer_standing='reuses_canonical' and mutation_policy='overwrite' on card 4 -- and the gate refused all three, naming the legal domain each time. A designed mutant can be unconsciously shaped to the validator the author already believes in; an accidental one cannot. FIFTH NEGATIVE, ADDED AFTER IT FAILED AS DESIGNED AND TAUGHT ME SOMETHING: prose in artifacts_produced[].commit_or_etag, which the TO's artifacts_contract forbids. The SCHEMA ACCEPTS IT (0 errors) -- so on that axis the schema is not the enforcing instrument. proof-of-spec-check REFUSES it: "VIOLATION: artifact-resolution: ... carries commit_or_etag 'see the commit', which is neither PENDING-THIS-COMMIT nor a 7-40 hex commit-ish for a repo artifact", INVALID, rc=1 read UNPIPED.
mutant.expected: Every shaped negative REJECTED with at least one error; every positive card ACCEPTED with zero.
mutant.observed: 16 of 16 shaped negatives rejected across the 4 cards (4 per card). 4 of 4 positives accepted with 0 errors. 3 of 3 unplanned live mutants rejected, each with the legal enum printed. One further real defect was caught by the same gate rather than by me: prose inside an artifact.location.co_resident_stores[].id on card 2, refused by the schema's own pattern, fixed by moving the table UUID into note. A separate negative control on the CHECKER itself: substrate-card-check against a non-card file (a .py) returns rc=2, so its rc=0 on a card is discriminating and not a constant. AND A NAMED LIMIT OF THE INSTRUMENT, found by a sixth arm I ran because the fifth surprised me: a WELL-FORMED BUT NON-EXISTENT hash (40 hex of deadbeef) passes BOTH gates -- rc=0, VALID -- and is merely announced as '1 UNRESOLVED-HERE (commit not in local store; announced, not asserted)'. So the resolution layer discriminates FORM always and EXISTENCE only as an announcement. What makes my own rows sound is not that they passed, but that they sit on the counted side of that line: 'artifact-resolution: 4 resolved at pin / 1 pending-on-worktree / 0 UNRESOLVED-HERE'. Worth recording that the checker also refuses to let its alignment numbers be quoted from an invalid instance -- it prints that they are identical to a valid instance's and are not evidence of validity.
